103 |  * Data pages should be large.  The only time a page should be written to disk
104 |  * is when the writer needs to flush the page to disk because it has accumulated
105 |  * too much data.  Pages are not read in sequential order and if pages are too
106 |  * small then the seek overhead (or request overhead) will be problematic.  We
107 |  * generally advise that pages be at least 8MB or larger.
108 |  *
109 |  * ## Encodings
110 |  *
111 |  * Specific encodings are not part of this minimal format.  They are provided
112 |  * by extensions. Readers and writers should be designed so that encodings can
113 |  * be easily added and removed. Ideally, they should allow for this without
114 |  * requiring recompilation through some kind of plugin system.
115 |  */
116 |
samples.review_note: Page grouping and eight-megabyte size are advice; dynamic plugin support is expressed as an ideal, not an implemented registry.

samples.claim: Equality fixture builds alternating bitmaps of lengths48 through55 from both full and empty constructors and asserts equality. This covers final-byte padding normalization together with logical bits; equality derives over both data and len.
samples.review_note: Lengths 48 through 55 and alternating constructors/clears match. Fresh Bitmap declaration and constructors confirm equality includes data/len and full-constructor padding is cleared.

samples.claim: new_with_old_frags walks destination tuples in caller order, skips zero-row destinations, appends (ID,current prefix,row count), and adds to total destination rows using ordinary u64 arithmetic. It clones the treemap bitmaps into an IntMap, collects old fragment metadata and creates a seen-fragment set. No destination-ID uniqueness or reserved-ID check occurs here; destination ranges are positional, so duplicate destination IDs can alias resulting physical addresses.
samples.review_note: Destination ordering, zero skip, prefix arithmetic and cloned bitmaps match. Fresh remainder/helper reads confirm old-fragment uniqueness checks but no destination uniqueness check, and physical address construction can alias duplicate destination IDs.

samples.claim: Public async-trait MappingReader requires Send+Sync+Debug+DeepSizeOf. Despite row_id names, the contract explicitly says physical addresses. remap_row_id(&self,u64)->Result<Option<u64>> returns mapped address or None for deleted source row; addresses outside source fragments or outside their valid offset ranges must return InvalidInput. Persisted invalid mappings should produce CorruptFile and storage errors propagate. These error requirements are an interface contract; the trait cannot enforce every implementation.
